definitions.explanation: The state or act of consuming an excessive amount of a beverage, most commonly alcohol. Very common in everyday conversation, especially when describing hangover-related situations.

examples.japanese: {飲|の}みすぎに{注意|ちゅうい}。
examples.english: Be careful not to drink too much.

examples.japanese: {昨日|きのう}は{飲|の}みすぎて{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}い。
examples.english: I drank too much yesterday and have a headache.

examples.japanese: {飲|の}みすぎは{体|からだ}に{悪|わる}いとわかっていても、つい{飲|の}んでしまう。
examples.english: Even though I know drinking too much is bad for my health, I end up drinking anyway.

notes:
The noun form of {飲|の}みすぎる (to drink too much), used to describe the state or act of excessive drinking. Most commonly refers to alcohol, but can also apply to any beverage. Very common in everyday conversation, especially the morning after a night out.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {飲|の}みすぎに{注意|ちゅうい}する: to be careful about overdrinking
- {飲|の}みすぎで{気持|きも}ち{悪|わる}い: feeling sick from drinking too much
- {飲|の}みすぎた: drank too much (past tense of the verb form)

RELATED WORDS:
- {食|た}べすぎ — overeating (same ~すぎ pattern)
- {二日酔|ふつかよ}い — hangover (a common result of {飲|の}みすぎ)
- {深酒|ふかざけ} — heavy drinking (more literary)
